title: Leveraging fructose transport to create a privileged substrate to selectively fuel T cells
text:
It has been shown that T-cell therapies are hindered by a dearth of metabolic precursors in the tumor
microenvironment. In this work, we will develop newly engineered T cells that can kill tumors leveraging a
nutrient available in the tumor microenvironment from our diet, fructose, and also novel strategies to image
fructose metabolism to provide imaging metabolic biomarkers of tumor metabolism and treatment response.
This work will advance the treatment of a range of solid tumors and develop non-invasive metabolic
biomarkers for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Yale-UNC Head and Neck Cancer SPORE: Overcoming Treatment Resistance in Head and Neck Cancer
text:
OVERALL NARRATIVE
The Yale-UNC Head and Neck SPORE is a team of clinical and laboratory researchers studying the problem of
treatment resistance in head and neck cancer. Each of four projects brings a basic and clinical research leader
working together to study ways to overcome resistance to common therapies, such as cetuximab, as well as to
find ways to make head and neck cancers more sensitive to immunotherapy. The projects are supported by core
facilities to provide administrative, pathology and statistical support, and there are funds to support new projects
and new investigators.

title: Differential function and tumor vulnerabilities revealed by RAS membrane trafficking
text:
RAS genes are mutated in human cancer more frequently than any other and the
proteins they encode require association with cellular membranes to function. Over the
past two decades we have studied the mechanisms that allow RAS to associate with
membranes and now propose to build on this work to identify vulnerabilities that can be
exploited in the development of novel anti-cancer therapies.

title: Data-driven biomolecular structure modeling for cryo-EM maps
text:
Cryo-electron microscopy is an emerging technique for determining the three-dimensional structure of
biological macromolecules. I will continue to develop computational methods that can accurately and
effectively model and interpret structures of biomolecules embedded in electron microscopy density maps and
thereby facilitate the understanding of molecular mechanisms of protein function and disease.

title: Integrating imaging and multi-omics data to infer single-cell 3D genome structures
text:
We will develop integrative methods for inferring high-resolution single cell genome structures from sparse
imaging and multi-omics data. We will analyze the 3D genome structures to derive structure-Function mapping.
The computational methods and the functional insights will deepen our knowledge in gene regulations and
cellular activities.

title: Treg-mediated tolerance of dystrophin immunity
text:
This study seeks to define the role of Dys-specific T cells in the context of adeno-associated virus-
microdystrophin (AAV-µDys) gene therapy for DMD patients. This study will explore the use of novel biologics
that selectively target and expand regulatory T cells (Tregs) as a therapeutic approach that inhibits Dys-
specific T cells and promotes dystrophin tolerance in DMD patients.

title: Tubulinopathy and visual disorders
text: Microtubules are ubiquitous cytoskeletal filaments essential for the function of eukaryotic cells. These polymers comprising -tubulin heterodimers are critical for diverse cellular functions, including ciliogenesis. The functional diversity of microtubules is attributed to the incorporation of various - and -tubulin isotypes, each encoded by different genes. Mutations in human tubulin genes have been linked to various tissue specific diseases, suggesting unique functions for each isotype. Specifically, mutations in the 4B-tubulin gene (TUBB4B) are associated with sensorineural hearing loss and Leber Congenital Amaurosis, a severe childhood blindness. Currently, therapeutic options for tubulinopathies are limited. Consequently, there is a critical need to develop tractable animal models to explore pathomechanisms and potential therapeutic interventions. Existing Tubb4b mouse models do not exhibit visual impairment, limiting the potential to address visual deficits associated with tubulinopathy. To address the gap, we performed CRISPR-mediated tubulin knockdown in zebrafish, which resulted in impaired retinal development and visual function. This finding demonstrates that zebrafish provide a tractable model for studying visual impairment in tubulinopathy. Our immediate objectives are: 1) to develop a stable zebrafish tubb4b model and 2) to determine how distinct tubulin isotypes contribute to retinal function. This project will generate a novel zebrafish model to assess the need for TUBB4B, a protein linked to blindness, in the retina. This proposal builds the foundation for an R01 submission where we will be well positioned to address how 1) specific tubulin isoforms impact photoreceptor physiology and structure, 2) specific tubulin alleles associated with tubulinopathy impact the retina and vision, and 3) screen drugs that improve retinal phenotypes in our model. These aims align with the National Eye Institute's strategic plan, specifically Area of Emphasis #1, From Genes to Disease Mechanisms. We are modeling genetic blindness linked to tubulin in zebrafish to elucidate the mechanisms behind the disease, which is fundamental knowledge needed to develop therapeutic strategies.

title: Mass Spectrometric Tissue Imaging of Sugars, Glycans, and Glycoconjugates
text:
The goal of this project is to establish mass spectrometry imaging capability to enable the more accurate and
comprehensive characterization of glycome (the entire carbohydrate repertoire) at near single-cell resolution.
This capability will incorporate a series of innovative advancements to mass spectrometry imaging, ion mobility,
ion activation, on-tissue chemical derivatization and enzymatic digestion, glycan enrichment, and micro-
processing of small amounts of material to overcome current limitations in glycome spatial analysis. The ability
to map the dynamic and heterogeneity of glycome to tissue functional units and cells will greatly assist in
identifying carbohydrate structures underpinning cellular function in the tissue context.

title: Circadian SCN-Liver Axis in the Neuroendocrine Response to Calorie Restriction
text:
A major function of the circadian system is to align feeding and metabolic cycles to optimize nutrient storage and
utilization across the light/dark cycle, though how the clock senses changes in nutrient availability to maintain
metabolic homeostasis throughout the day is not well-understood. The major goals of our proposed studies are
(i) to dissect the mechanisms underlying the role of the clock at the level of liver and brain in maintaining energy
constancy during fasting/sleep, and (ii) to dissect the molecular basis for nutrient sensing by the clock that
underlies the physiologic adaptation to healthful calorie restriction. Results from the proposed studies will
elucidate how the clock sustains the vital provision of energy to brain during sleep and how calorie restriction
acts through the clock to improve health.

title: Resubmission: A Mechanistic Study to Investigate tDCS and Working Memory in MCI Patients
text:
Working memory, a sub-cognitive domain that provides temporary storage of memory to perform complex
cognitive tasks, is essential for maintaining activities of daily living and one of the first functions to decline
in older adults with cognitive impairments including Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia. The proposed
project and the training components associated with this project will examine working memory gains induced
by transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) as a cognitive intervention method in cognitively healthy
and impaired cohorts. Results from this study will promote a better understanding of mechanistic properties
underlying working memory gains with tDCS and guide future intervention strategies to combat cognitive
decline and improve the quality of life of aging and dementia populations.

title: OFC Astrocytes and Ethanol
text:
Identifying factors that underlie the development of excessive alcohol consumption is critical for
developing effective treatments for alcohol use disorder. In this application, we focus on
astrocytes in the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) and how they contribute to changes in OFC neuron
excitability and control over alcohol drinking.

title: Mapping endogenous protein dynamics in living cells
text:
This project aims at developing microscopy and computational platforms for the analysis of mammalian cell
libraries with endogenously tagged proteins. These new tools will enable proteome-wide analysis of protein
localization and interaction networks in a native cellular context.

title: The role and mechanism of alternative RNA splice variants and gene fusions as drivers of cancer
text:
Human brain tumors are genomic heterogeneous within the tumor population and very large datasets of clinical
and molecular data on large numbers of patients have been created. Over the past 25 years, my laboratory
has worked on modeling brain tumors in mice and correlating those findings with data from human brain tumor
patients and have developed unique big data visualization tools that allow the interactive interpretation of these
data. We are now using our mouse modeling technology to understand the biology of rare tumors driven by
gene fusions and the role of RNA splicing variants of TrkB in development and oncogenesis.

title: Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging for non-invasive breast cancer therapy using physics-informed neural networks.
text:
Breast cancer is the most diagnosed cancer worldwide, accounting for an estimated 12% of all cancer
cases in 2020, with promising noninvasive treatments under active development. This proposal aims to
develop physics-informed machine learning and magnetic resonance imaging techniques for evaluating
noninvasive focused ultrasound treatments for breast cancer. Development of these techniques will provide
efficient breast MRI exams for clinical use, support the collection of images to evaluate focused ultrasound
breast cancer treatments, and advance current understanding of applying machine learning models to
magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Physiological Characterization of PBN CGRP Neurons During Chronic Opioid Exposure and Withdrawal
text:
Opioid withdrawal leads to somatic symptoms and aversive states – both of which activate neuronal circuits
involved in processing aversive experiences. The external lateral parabrachial nucleus (elPBN), which houses a
calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) population, is known to be a critical hub for relaying information about
aversive experiences and, therefore, may be a compelling region for studying opioid withdrawal. This project
aims to determine if elPBNCGRP neurons play an important role in opioid withdrawal, ultimately determining if the
CGRP population is a targetable population for therapeutics.

title: Role of vesicular trafficking proteins in regulating centrosomes
text:
This application requests an administrative supplement to the parent NIGMS R15
research award 7R15GM152965-02 to purchase a LI-COR Odyssey XF Imaging Bundle —
Basic that will replace an unreliable end-of-life LI-COR Odyssey Fc imaging system. The
requested equipment is essential for completing the approved parent project investigating how
vesicular trafficking proteins regulate centrosomes. Successful completion of this project will
advance fundamental knowledge of centrosome biology and cell division, processes relevant to
human diseases including neurodevelopmental disorders and cancer.

title: Iron Trafficking and Regulation in Biological Systems
text:
Iron and copper are essential for human health but they can also damage cells and entire organs.
Thus, understanding how these metals are imported into our bodies and cells, and how they move
within cells, is highly significant. In this project we will characterize metal “trafficking” and
regulation in cells and in the blood, with the ultimate aim of developing better treatments for metal-
related diseases.

title: RNA Recombination in Coronaviruses
text: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is the etiological agent responsible for COVID19 disease in the current pandemic. RNA recombination is required during normal replication to generate subgenomic mRNAs required for protein expression, gives rise defective viral RNAs and generates numerous structural variants that facilitate adaption and evolution of SARS-CoV-2. We will characterize the molecular mechanisms that determine the sites and rates of RNA recombination and learn how selection in different physiological environments results in the selection and emergence of novel variants of SARS-CoV-2.

title: Cellular Determinants of HCMV infection
text:
Human Cytomegalovirus (HCMV) causes permanent neuronal damage in thousands of infants in the United
States every year and is responsible for significant disease and death in individuals with weakened immune
systems, including transplant recipients and some cancer patients. Our proposal focuses on understanding the
mechanisms by which a viral protein, UL26, modulates the activity of JUNB, a cellular transcription factor. Our
results suggest that in the absence of UL26, JUNB induces an anti-viral state to inhibit viral replication.
Understanding the mechanisms through which these cellular proteins impact infection could pave the way for
novel therapeutic strategies to combat viral pathogenesis.

title: Structured quantification of inherited macular disease phenotypes as the basis for automated algorithms to determine causal genes
text:
The ability to obtain a molecular diagnosis in patients is essential for understanding the cellular etiology, clinical
prognosis, and treatment prospects of inherited macular dystrophy —a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders
characterized by progressive central vision loss. Genetic testing has recently become more accessible to
patients with IMD, however, testing outcomes are often inconclusive due to the difficult task of identifying a single
causal gene across the immense and complex landscape of the human genome. Using advanced diagnostic
retinal imaging modalities, this research proposal will decipher precise phenotypic differences between IMD
genes and create a prediction tool to help improve genetic testing outcomes for patients.
